description:
FILED s451 (Fable, round-10 companion attribution).  op/rt119311.t 9/2 -> 9/0: perl rows 10/11 ("exit triggering DESTROY directly inside format" / "...that calls outer format") used to produce not-ok verdicts and now the file STOPS at row 9 ("planned 22 ran 9") -- a 2-row coverage LOSS, the only negative-coverage member of the #542 companion family.

ATTRIBUTED by merge-point bisect (do not redo): 718db6b = 9/2; 80a11a7 (agent X, #542 stdio buffering + PERL_FLUSHALL_FOR_CHILD + exit-hook flush) = 9/0; identical at 4b7540b and c880cd9.  The aborted-forms note is IDENTICAL both sides ("Can t find label test" x2), so the change is that row 10 s own form now dies/aborts where it used to complete with a wrong value.  The row-10 shape involves `exit` triggered from DESTROY inside a format -- exactly the path #542 touched (exit hooks now flush; p-exit reaches sb-ext:exit).

NEXT DISCRIMINATOR (not yet taken): run the file with PCL_SUITE_KEEP and read the kept transpile stderr + raw output tail for the row-10 form; then probe the minimal shape (format + DESTROY calling exit) under ./pcl direct vs perl, on c880cd9 and on 718db6b.  Suspects in order: an in-process exit in the row-10 child/eval now terminates the parent (the recovered die became a real exit); the exit-hook flush re-entering output machinery during DESTROY-in-format.

BAR: rows 10/11 produce verdicts again (not-ok is fine -- they were failing before); the file back to >= 9/2 with the mechanism named; snapshot row re-spliced with the true cause.

DONE s452aa (Opus agent AA, round 11).  MECHANISM NAMED AND FIXED; the file is
BETTER than the pre-#542 reading.

THE MECHANISM (measured, not inferred).  The task's first suspect was right in
substance and the discriminator was a two-line SBCL probe, not the kept
artifacts:

    (push (lambda () (print "hook start") (sb-ext:exit :code 7)
                     (print "hook after")) sb-ext:*exit-hooks*)

  On SBCL 2.6.0 that prints "hook start", exits 7, and NEVER prints "hook
  after": a NESTED sb-ext:exit inside a running exit hook goes straight to the
  OS and ABANDONS THE REST OF THE HOOK.

PCL runs END blocks from exactly such a hook, and the hook is
    (dolist (fn *end-blocks*) â¦)  then  (%p-flush-all-output)
so an `exit` inside any END block killed BOTH the remaining END blocks AND the
flush.  Minimal repro, three END blocks with `exit 7` in the middle:

    perl   main / END-C / END-B exiting / END-A code=7   rc=7
    PCL    main                                          rc=0     (before)

-- i.e. even END-C, which had ALREADY RUN, was lost, because its text was
sitting in STDOUT's block buffer.  That is the #542 dependency: before #542 a
line-buffered STDOUT had already pushed those lines out, so the same defect cost
nothing visible.  With `$| = 1` the pre-fix run prints main/END-C/END-B and
stops, which separates the two halves cleanly (the flush loss and the
remaining-ENDs loss).

PERL'S RULE, PROBED: `exit` inside an END block ends THAT BLOCK.  Every
remaining END still runs, reads the status as `$?`, and the process finally
exits with it.

FIX (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp):
  *p-in-end-phase* / *p-end-phase-pid* / *p-end-exit-code* (new defvars, with
  the mechanism written down beside them).
  The exit hook binds the first two, wraps each block in (catch '%p-end-exit â¦)
  inside the existing handler-case, and AFTER the loop and AFTER
  %p-flush-all-output exits with the recorded status if there is one -- last,
  precisely because that nested exit abandons whatever follows it.
  p-exit, when in the END phase AND in the process that entered it, records the
  status, sets $?, and throws.  THE PID GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING: a fork child
  created by an END block inherits the binding and must still exit for real.

RESULT: op/rt119311.t 9/0 -> 11/2 (parallel and serial agree; "REAL MOVE").
  rows 10/11 (`exit triggering DESTROY directly inside format` / `â¦ that calls
  outer format`) come back as not-ok -- the two rows the flush had eaten, which
  is what the task asked for -- and rows 12/13 (`â¦ that calls current sub` /
  `â¦ that calls outer sub`) are NEW PASSES produced by the remaining-ENDs
  semantics.  EXPECTED SNAPSHOT MOVEMENT for Fable to splice:
      op/rt119311.t  C_ok 9 -> 11,  C_notok 0 -> 2   (was 9/2 pre-#542)
  Everything else about the row (P 22/0, verdict DIFF, the aborted-forms note)
  is unchanged.

GUARDS: Pl/t/stdio-buffering-01.t 11 -> 13 rows -- the END-exit row (through a
PIPE, which is where the buffer is what carries the text) and its inverse (a
top-level exit still stops the program).  Both compare against perl.

RESIDUE FILED: #741 -- `./runpcl` reports rc=0 for a program that exits 7.  The
emitted CL is right (direct SBCL gives 7); the wrapper drops the status.  Found
because the first exit-code check of this fix read 0 from runpcl and 7 from
SBCL for the same file.
